title: Act V, Scene II

teacherSummary.text: Friar John tells Friar Laurence that he was quarantined and could not deliver the letter. Friar Laurence hurries to the tomb.

vocabulary.context:
Unhappy fortune! by my brotherhood,
The letter was not nice but full of charge
Of dear import, and the neglecting it
May do much danger.

writingPrompts.label: HS Freshman

writingPrompts.label: HS Sophomore
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how Act V, Scene II develops the idea of the undelivered letter. Make a precise claim, support it with at least three pieces of textual evidence, and explain how the author's use of plot and irony shapes that idea. Address one possible counterclaim.

writingPrompts.label: HS Junior
writingPrompts.text: Analyze how the structure of Act V, Scene II (where it begins, turns and ends) and its plot shape the reader's understanding of the undelivered letter. Identify one place where the text leaves matters uncertain and explain how that uncertainty adds to its meaning.

writingPrompts.label: HS Senior
writingPrompts.text: Two readers disagree about what Act V, Scene II suggests about the undelivered letter. Lay out two plausible interpretations, weigh the evidence for each (including the scene's plot and irony), and argue for the stronger one in a sustained, well-organized essay.

writingPrompts.label: AP
writingPrompts.text: Write a literary argument in which you analyze how William Shakespeare uses plot in Act V, Scene II to complicate the reader's understanding of the undelivered letter. Develop a defensible thesis, select evidence purposefully, and explain how specific choices of diction and syntax create meaning.

writingPrompts.label: College Freshman
writingPrompts.text: Situate Act V, Scene II within its historical and literary context and argue how the scene's treatment of the undelivered letter responds to that context. Engage with at least one secondary perspective (a critic, historian or the author's own statements), integrate quotations smoothly, and cite in MLA style.

writingPrompts.label: College Sophomore
writingPrompts.text: Read Act V, Scene II alongside the conventions of its genre and period. Argue how the scene's handling of the undelivered letter follows or bends those conventions, using the plot as evidence, and test your reading against one published critic. Document two secondary sources in MLA.

writingPrompts.label: College Junior
writingPrompts.text: Apply a named critical approach (for example formalist, historicist, feminist, psychoanalytic or ecocritical) to Act V, Scene II and its treatment of the undelivered letter. State your method, show what it reveals in the scene's plot and irony, and identify where the text resists it.

writingPrompts.label: College Senior
writingPrompts.text: Develop a research argument that reads Act V, Scene II as evidence for a larger claim about the undelivered letter in Romeo and Juliet. Connect close reading of the scene to the whole play, engage at least four scholarly sources, and state precisely where your reading departs from theirs (Chicago style).

writingPrompts.label: Graduate / PhD
writingPrompts.text: Develop an original argument that reads Act V, Scene II as a hinge in the play's larger treatment of the undelivered letter. Position your reading within a named critical conversation (for example formalist, historicist, psychoanalytic, feminist or postcolonial approaches), account for the textual history where relevant, and articulate the stakes of your intervention for scholarship on Romeo and Juliet.

segments.script: Plague quarantines sealed houses. Chance undoes the plan. Plot: Friar John was quarantined and could not deliver the letter. Irony: A plague, not a person, stops the message. Characterization: Friar Laurence's urgency and plan to go to the tomb alone. Watch for fate and the stars: From "star-cross'd" in the Prologue to Romeo's "I defy you, stars," the lovers feel steered by fortune, while the plot shows human choices and accidents. In this scene: “Unhappy fortune! by my brotherhood, / The letter was not nice but full of” (Act V, Scene II, Friar Laurence).

objective: Students will summarize what happens in Act V, Scene II (the undelivered letter) in 2 sentences and, in a 3-sentence warm-up response, explain how one quoted line from the scene sets up the scene that follows.

routine: Bell-ringer: post one literal and one evaluative question; students jot before talking (wait time).
Discussion (10 min): run the focus questions for the class level in order, literal to evaluative; think-pair-share every DOK 3/4 item.
After each answer, use a follow-up probe before moving on; ask a second student to agree, extend or challenge.
Exit: each student writes one question of their own (student-generated) for tomorrow’s opener.
